steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Semiotics: the study of signs and symbols — everything on stage is a sign that carries meaning. | Key Fact: Denotation: what something literally is; connotation: what it suggests or symbolises. A red light denotes light colour but connotes danger, passion or hell. | Key Fact: Proxemics: the spatial relationship between characters — distance shows relationship, power or tension. | Key Fact: Blocking: the precise movement and positioning of actors on stage — every position is deliberate.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain the difference between denotation and connotation, using a specific example from a production you have seen. | How does a director use proxemics and levels to communicate the relationship between two characters? | Describe how semiotics helps an audience understand the deeper meaning of a performance.
